daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo accepted Gibran's resignation as Vice President, calling it a "statesman-like" decision after educational qualification issues emerged. Gibran thanked Prabowo in his first address since stepping down. The MPR leadership set a December 4 target to complete the selection of a replacement Vice President.

  • Prabowo will convene coalition parties to discuss two names to replace Gibran as Vice President.
  • PAN affirmed it will follow Prabowo's choice for the two vice presidential replacement candidates.
  • Bambang Pacul responded to speculation about Puan Maharani emerging as a potential Gibran replacement.
  • The West Java Education Office is awaiting central guidance before removing Gibran's photos from schools.
  • The MPR will hold a joint session to discuss the mechanism for filling the vacant Vice President seat.
  • The Constitutional Court declined to accept a challenge to regulations on educational certificate requirements for presidential and vice presidential candidates.
  • PBNU called on all state institutions to safeguard the integrity of the Republic.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia pressed developed nations to meet climate finance targets at the COP31 conference. Indonesia also promoted forest fire control measures at global forums and received a US$100 million grant from Norway for successfully reducing deforestation.

  • Indonesia and Papua New Guinea expanded cross-border healthcare access between their territories.
  • Indonesia and Singapore are exploring a tax data exchange to curb corporate abuses.
  • Indonesia showcased an unmanned attack vessel during an amphibious exercise.
  • Indonesia aims to complete China trade pact negotiations by early 2029, according to Coordinating Minister Hartarto.
  • Germany urged Indonesia to cut tariffs and expand investment in industry and energy sectors.

Other

Indonesia's state budget recorded a deficit of Rp 379 trillion through October as government spending exceeded revenues. The government assured fuel subsidies remain safe despite the rupiah's weakness. Officials emphasized that Indonesia's economic fundamentals remain resilient.

  • The KPK stated that Puspom TNI has begun examining active military personnel in connection with BNPB corruption cases.
  • The tax directorate said Indonesia's PTKP is already relatively high and is considering potential revisions.
  • Indonesia raised the 2026 school revitalization target to 80,744 facilities.
  • The ESDM Ministry is reviewing B50 implementation after industry expressed concerns about raw material availability.
  • Indonesia seeks self-reliance in pharmaceutical raw materials, according to government officials.
